title: Heat and Cold: Cooling, Rewarming and the BC Rules
next: Chapter 38, Lesson 2: Drowning, diving and altitude emergencies

slides.title: Today's lesson
slides.body:
As an EMR you already move patients out of the heat or cold, remove wet clothing, cool, warm and give oxygen. Today, as a PCP:

  1. Understand how the body loses heat, and who fails first
  2. Sort heat illness; cool heatstroke right (BC: ≥ 10 min first)
  3. Grade frostbite and hypothermia, rewarm the BC way, run a cold arrest

Textbook: Chapter 38, PDF pages 3241–3287
slides.say: Welcome to Chapter 38. Environmental emergencies are caused or made worse by the weather, the terrain, or the air and water around us. In Canada, about eighty people die of hypothermia each year, and about twelve hundred deaths are linked to heat. As EMRs, you already move patients out of the heat or cold and remove wet clothing. As a PCP, you need the reasons behind the care. Today we'll cover how the body loses heat, how to sort heat illness and cool heatstroke properly, and how to grade frostbite and hypothermia and manage them the BC way, including a cold cardiac arrest.
slides.sayZh: 欢迎来到第三十八章。环境急症是由天气、地形或周围的空气和水引起或加重的。在加拿大，每年约八十人死于低体温，约一千二百例死亡与高温有关。作为 EMR，你们已经会把病人移出高温或寒冷环境、脱掉湿衣服。作为 PCP，你要明白处置背后的道理。今天讲：身体怎样散热；怎样区分热病、正确地给热射病降温；以及怎样给冻伤和低体温分级，并按 BC 方式处理，包括低体温心脏骤停。

slides.title: Four ways to lose heat
slides.body:
Core ≈ 37 °C; the hypothalamus is the thermostat

RouteKey factOn scene
Radiation> 65% of loss in a cool settingcover the head, esp. infants
Conductionwater: 25× faster than airoff wet clothes, off the ground
Convectionmoving air or waterwind chill; fans cool
Evaporationsweat; stops near 75% humiditywet skin + fan for heatstroke

When the air is as warm as the skin, only sweating works.
slides.say: The body keeps its core near thirty-seven degrees, and the hypothalamus in the brain is the thermostat. Heat leaves in four ways. Radiation is heat given off to the air; in a cool place it's over sixty-five percent of heat loss, much of it from the head, especially in babies. Conduction is direct contact; water pulls heat away about twenty-five times faster than air, so wet clothes and cold ground are dangerous. Convection is moving air carrying heat away: that's wind chill, and it's why fans help in heatstroke. Evaporation is sweat drying, but it stops working at about seventy-five percent humidity.
slides.sayZh: 身体把核心体温维持在三十七度左右，大脑里的下丘脑就是恒温器。热量通过四条途径散失。辐射是向空气散发热量，在凉爽环境中占散热的百分之六十五以上，很多从头部散失，婴儿尤其如此。传导是直接接触，水带走热量的速度约是空气的二十五倍，所以湿衣服和冰冷的地面很危险。对流是流动的空气把热量带走，这就是风寒效应，也是热射病时用风扇有效的原因。蒸发是汗液变干，但湿度到百分之七十五左右就不起作用了。

slides.title: Heat illness: a spectrum
slides.body:
Heat crampssalt loss; painful crampsalert, temp normal
Heat exhaustionvolume loss + heat stresstemp normal or < 40 °C; pale, sweaty, dizzy
Heatstrokecore > 40 °C + altered mental statusleast common, deadliest
  • Cramps: sip an electrolyte drink; no salt tablets, no massage
  • Exhaustion: cool place, lie flat, legs up; BP may drop on standing
  • Higher risk: elderly, infants, athletes; diuretics, beta blockers

Can't tell exhaustion from heatstroke? Treat it as heatstroke.
slides.say: Heat illness is a spectrum. At the mild end are heat cramps: painful cramps after heavy sweating, when the patient replaced water but not salt. They're alert, with a normal temperature. Give an electrolyte drink to sip and a salty snack, but no salt tablets and no massage. In the middle is heat exhaustion: low volume plus heat stress. The patient is pale, sweaty, dizzy, maybe a little confused, with a temperature below forty. At the far end is heatstroke: a core temperature above forty plus an altered mental status. If you can't tell exhaustion from heatstroke, treat it as heatstroke.
slides.sayZh: 热病是一个连续谱。最轻的一端是热痉挛：大量出汗后只补了水、没补盐，引起疼痛性抽筋。病人清醒，体温正常。给电解质饮料慢慢喝，配点咸零食，但不给盐片，也不按摩。中间是热衰竭：容量不足加上热应激。病人苍白、出汗、头晕，可能有点糊涂，体温低于四十度。最重的一端是热射病：核心体温高于四十度，加上精神状态改变。分不清热衰竭和热射病时，按热射病处理。

slides.title: Heatstroke: classic or exertional
slides.body:
ClassicExertional
Whoolder, chronically ill, bedriddenyoung, fit, exercising hard
Sweatmay be absentusually present
Skinhot, red, drypale, moist
Glucosenormal or highlow
Muscle breakdown, kidney failurerarecommon

Early signs: odd behaviour, confusion; pupils usually small. Sweating does not rule it out.
slides.say: There are two types of heatstroke. Classic heatstroke strikes older, chronically ill or bedridden people during heat waves; their skin may be hot, red and dry because sweating has stopped. Exertional heatstroke hits young, fit people exercising hard. They usually still sweat, with pale, moist skin, and they're often hypoglycemic. Rhabdomyolysis, which is muscle breakdown, and kidney failure are common. So a sweating patient can still have heatstroke. The earliest signs are often behaviour changes, like irritability, combativeness or hallucinations, easily mistaken for drugs or a psychiatric problem. Pupils are usually small. In hot weather, anyone acting strangely needs a core temperature.
slides.sayZh: 热射病有两型。经典型在热浪期间袭击老人、慢性病人或卧床者，因为已经不出汗，皮肤可能又热又红又干。劳力型见于剧烈运动的年轻健康人，他们通常还在出汗，皮肤苍白潮湿，而且常有低血糖；横纹肌溶解（也就是肌肉分解）和肾衰竭很常见。所以，还在出汗的病人也可能是热射病。最早的表现常是行为改变，比如易激惹、攻击性、幻觉，很容易被误认为药物或精神问题。瞳孔通常偏小。天热时，任何行为怪异的人都要测核心体温。

slides.q: A 23-year-old runner collapses near the finish line on a hot, humid day. He is confused and combative, still sweating, with pale skin. Core temperature is 40.8 °C. What is the best plan?
options: He is sweating, so it's heat exhaustion: oral fluids and rest
Load and go now; cooling can wait for the hospital
Cool aggressively on scene for at least 10 minutes, then transport while cooling
Ice packs on the neck and groin only, then transport
slides.say: Let's check. A twenty-three-year-old runner collapses near the finish line on a hot, humid day. He's confused and combative, still sweating, with pale skin. His core temperature is forty point eight degrees. What's the best plan? A, he's sweating, so it's heat exhaustion: give oral fluids and rest. B, load and go now; cooling can wait for the hospital. C, cool him aggressively on scene for at least ten minutes, then transport while you keep cooling. D, ice packs on the neck and groin only, then transport. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 检查一下。一位二十三岁的跑者在炎热潮湿的天气里倒在终点附近，意识混乱、有攻击性，还在出汗，皮肤苍白，核心体温四十点八度。最好的方案是什么？A 他在出汗，所以是热衰竭：口服补液、休息；B 马上装车走，降温等到医院再说；C 在现场积极降温至少十分钟，然后一边转运一边继续降温；D 只在颈部和腹股沟放冰袋，然后转运。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is C. A core temperature above forty with an altered mental status is heatstroke, and sweating doesn't rule it out in exertional heatstroke. BC says cool for at least ten minutes before you start transport, then keep using the most aggressive cooling method on the way. A misses a deadly diagnosis. B skips the cooling that protects the brain. D is too weak, because ice packs alone don't cool well; they only add to water and fanning.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 C。核心体温高于四十度加上精神状态改变就是热射病；劳力型热射病有汗也不能排除。BC 规定开始转运前至少降温十分钟，路上继续用最积极的降温方法。A 漏掉了致命的诊断；B 跳过了保护大脑的降温；D 力度太弱，单用冰袋降温效果差，只能作为喷水加扇风的补充。

slides.title: Cooling heatstroke: what works
slides.body:
• Best: ice-water immersion; ice-water towels + fanning come close
  • Good: spray tepid water and fan
  • Weak alone: ice packs, dry fanning, cooling blankets, a wet sheet on top
  • Cool place, remove all clothing, AC on maximum cold
  • Cold wet towels on head, torso, thighs; feet and legs in ice water
  • Cool at least 10 min before transport; keep cooling en route

Book: check rectal or tympanic temp every 10 min; stop at < 39 °C to avoid overshoot.
slides.say: How do you cool heatstroke? The book's evidence says ice-water immersion works best, and ice-water-soaked towels with fanning come close. On their own, ice packs, dry fanning, cooling blankets, or a wet sheet laid on top don't work well. The BC protocol puts this into practice: a cool place, all clothing off, air conditioning on maximum cold, cold wet towels on the head, torso and thighs, and the feet and legs in ice water. Cool for at least ten minutes before transport, and keep cooling on the way. The book stops at thirty-nine degrees to avoid overshooting into shivering.
slides.sayZh: 热射病怎么降温？原书的证据显示冰水浸泡效果最好，冰水浸湿的毛巾加扇风接近它；单用冰袋、干扇风、降温毯，或在身上盖一张湿床单，效果都不好。BC 流程把这些落到实处：移到凉爽处、脱掉全部衣服、空调开到最冷、头部躯干和大腿敷冷湿毛巾、双脚和小腿泡冰水。转运前至少降温十分钟，路上继续降温。原书降到三十九度就停，以免降过头引起寒战。

slides.title: Frostbite: superficial or deep?
slides.body:
SuperficialDeep
Feelfirm surface, soft underneathhard, cold, numb
Lookwhite, waxywhite, yellow-white, blotchy blue
Carebody heat: warm hand, or hand in armpit~1 h from hospital: keep it frozen, pad it
  • Never rub, massage, or use dry or radiant heat
  • Never thaw a part that could refreeze
  • Long delay: medical control; 35–40 °C water bath, 10–30 min

Not sure? Treat it as deep.
slides.say: Frostbite is frozen tissue, usually fingers, toes, ears, nose or cheeks. In superficial frostbite, the skin is white, waxy and firm, but the tissue underneath is still soft. Rewarm it with body heat: a warm hand on the ear or nose, or the patient's hand held still in their armpit. Deep frostbite is hard, cold and numb all the way through. If you're about an hour or less from hospital, keep it frozen, pad it, and keep it away from the heater. Refreezing does even more damage, so never thaw a part that could refreeze. Never rub or massage frostbite. Not sure? Treat it as deep.
slides.sayZh: 冻伤就是组织被冻住，常见于手指、脚趾、耳朵、鼻子和面颊。浅表冻伤的皮肤白、像蜡、摸着硬，但下面的组织还是软的。用体温复温：用温暖的手捂住耳朵或鼻子，或让病人把手放在腋下不动。深部冻伤从表到里都又硬又冷又麻木。如果离医院大约一小时以内，就保持冻结状态，垫好保护，远离暖气。再次冻结的伤害更大，所以可能再冻结的部位绝不解冻。冻伤绝不能搓揉或按摩。拿不准时，按深部冻伤处理。

slides.title: Hypothermia: the cold body slows down
slides.body:
• Core temp < 35 °C; can happen indoors at 15.5 °C
  • Early: the "umbles": stumbles, mumbles, fumbles, grumbles
  • Mimics stroke, head injury, drunkenness: take a core temp
  • Cold diuresis + fluid shifts → thick blood, low volume
  • Shivering burns glucose → hypoglycemia; drugs last longer
  • Big risks: alcohol, old age, infants, trauma
slides.say: Hypothermia means a core temperature below thirty-five degrees, and it doesn't need snow. An older person living alone can become hypothermic in a house at about fifteen degrees. Early signs are the umbles: the patient stumbles, mumbles, fumbles and grumbles. Because the brain slows down, hypothermia is easily mistaken for a stroke, a head injury or drunkenness, so take a core temperature. The kidneys make extra urine, called cold diuresis, so the blood thickens and the volume drops. Shivering burns glucose, so check the sugar. Alcohol is the most common contributor, but trauma matters most: injured patients can't shiver well and bleed more when cold.
slides.sayZh: 低体温指核心体温低于三十五度，并不一定要有雪。独居老人在大约十五度的屋里就可能低体温。早期表现是几个「umbles」：走不稳、说话含糊、手脚笨拙、爱发牢骚。因为大脑变慢，低体温很容易被误认为卒中、颅脑外伤或醉酒，所以要测核心体温。肾脏会多产尿，叫冷利尿，于是血液变稠、容量下降。寒战消耗葡萄糖，所以要测血糖。酒精是最常见的诱因，但创伤最要紧：受伤的人寒战不好，体温低时出血也更多。

slides.title: Hypothermia grades and BC rewarming
slides.body:
Mild32–35 °C: shivering, umblesBC: actively rewarm
Moderate28–32 °C: shivering stops; arrhythmiasBC: actively rewarm
Severe< 28 °C: high VF riskBC: insulate only, handle gently
  • Active (BC): cab preheated to 30 °C, hot packs in towels, warm blankets
  • Watch for afterdrop: core keeps falling as cold limb blood returns
slides.say: BC uses three grades. Mild is thirty-two to thirty-five degrees: the patient shivers and has the umbles. Moderate is twenty-eight to thirty-two: shivering stops, and rhythm problems such as atrial fibrillation begin. Severe is below twenty-eight, where the heart can easily go into ventricular fibrillation. For mild and moderate, BC says rewarm actively: preheat the ambulance to thirty degrees, use hot packs wrapped in towels, warm blankets, and mild activity if appropriate. For severe hypothermia, do not actively rewarm: insulate, keep the ambulance at thirty, and handle the patient gently. Also watch for afterdrop, when cold blood from the limbs keeps lowering the core temperature.
slides.sayZh: BC 分三级。轻度是三十二到三十五度：病人寒战，有那些「umbles」。中度是二十八到三十二度：寒战停止，开始出现房颤等心律问题。重度低于二十八度，心脏很容易发生室颤。轻度和中度，BC 规定主动复温：救护车预热到三十度、用毛巾包好的热敷包、暖毯，合适时做轻度活动。重度低体温不主动复温：隔绝保温，车厢保持三十度，轻柔搬动病人。还要警惕复温后续降：四肢的冷血回流，让核心体温继续下降。

slides.title: Cold cardiac arrest: the BC rules
slides.body:
• Check the pulse for up to 30–45 seconds
  • AED: up to 3 shocks, then CPR with no pauses to analyze or shock
  • Rapid transport; CPR during transport is allowed for hypothermia
  • Book: VF rarely converts below 30 °C
  • Book: fixed pupils, stiffness, lividity are not reasons to stop
  • Book: stop only for lethal injuries or a chest too frozen to compress
slides.say: Now the cold cardiac arrest, where BC has its own rules. A severely hypothermic patient can have a very slow, weak pulse, so take up to thirty to forty-five seconds to confirm it's absent. In arrest, apply the AED and shock up to three times if advised. After that, keep doing CPR without pausing to analyze or shock, and transport rapidly; BC allows CPR during transport for hypothermia. Why? The book explains that a very cold heart rarely responds to shocks below thirty degrees. The book also says don't give up early: fixed pupils, stiffness and lividity are not reasons to stop. Only lethal injuries, or a chest too frozen to compress, are.
slides.sayZh: 再看低体温心脏骤停，BC 有专门规定。重度低体温病人的脉搏可能又慢又弱，所以要用最多三十到四十五秒确认没有脉搏。骤停时贴上 AED，建议除颤就最多电击三次；之后持续 CPR，不再停下来分析或电击，并快速转运；BC 允许低体温病人在转运中做 CPR。为什么？原书解释说，体温低于三十度时，很冷的心脏对电击很少有反应。原书还说，别太早放弃：瞳孔固定、身体僵硬和尸斑都不是停止的理由；只有致命伤，或胸壁冻到无法按压，才是。

slides.q: A man is found in a snowbank. He is pulseless after a 45-second check. The AED has delivered 3 shocks and still advises a shock. What do you do now?
options: Keep analyzing every 2 minutes and shock whenever advised
Continue CPR without pausing to analyze or shock, and transport rapidly
Stop resuscitation: his pupils are fixed and dilated
Rewarm him on scene first, then restart the AED
slides.say: Another question. A man is found in a snowbank. He's pulseless after a forty-five-second check. The AED has delivered three shocks and is still advising a shock. What do you do now? A, keep analyzing every two minutes and shock whenever it's advised. B, continue CPR without pausing to analyze or shock, and transport rapidly. C, stop resuscitation, because his pupils are fixed and dilated. D, rewarm him on scene first, then restart the AED. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 再来一题。一名男子在雪堆里被发现，检查四十五秒没有脉搏。AED 已经电击三次，仍然提示电击。现在怎么做？A 继续每两分钟分析一次，提示就电击；B 持续 CPR，不再停下来分析或电击，并快速转运；C 停止复苏，因为他瞳孔固定散大；D 先在现场复温，再重新使用 AED。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is B. In the BC hypothermia protocol, you defibrillate up to three times, then continue CPR with no pauses for analysis or shocks, and transport rapidly. A follows the usual arrest pattern, which BC changes for hypothermia. C is wrong because fixed, dilated pupils are not a reason to stop in severe hypothermia. D is wrong because BC says not to actively rewarm a severely hypothermic patient at all; this patient needs CPR and rapid transport.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 B。BC 低体温流程规定最多除颤三次，之后持续 CPR，不再为分析或电击暂停，并快速转运。A 是普通骤停的做法，而 BC 对低体温做了改变。C 错在重度低体温时瞳孔固定散大不是停止的理由。D 错在 BC 规定重度低体温病人根本不做主动复温；这个病人需要的是 CPR 和快速转运。

slides.title: EMR vs PCP: heat and cold
slides.body:
BC Heat Exhaustion/Heatstroke, Hypothermia and Diabetic Emergencies protocols

All licence levels (EMR + PCP)

  • Heat: cool place, strip, AC max cold, wet towels, ice-water feet
  • Heat: cool ≥ 10 min before transport; keep cooling en route
  • Heat: blood glucose if LOC is decreased
  • Cold: wet clothes off; pulse check up to 30–45 s
  • Cold: rewarm mild/moderate; severe: insulate, cab 30 °C
  • Cold arrest: AED up to 3 shocks, then CPR without pauses

PCP adds

  • Heat: consider IV fluids for signs of dehydration
  • Confirmed BGL < 4.0: IV D10W 10–25 g (glucagon if no IV)
  • Hypothermia: no PCP-only steps; same care at every level
  • Functional enquiry (PCP only)
slides.say: On the left is what every licence level does. For heat: a cool place, all clothing off, maximum air conditioning, cold wet towels, ice water for the feet, at least ten minutes of cooling before transport, and a blood sugar if consciousness is decreased. For cold: wet clothing off, a long pulse check, active rewarming for mild and moderate cases, insulation for severe, and the three-shock AED rule. On the right, the PCP adds IV fluids when a heat patient shows dehydration, and IV dextrose if the sugar is confirmed below four. The hypothermia protocol has no PCP-only steps; your value there is assessment and judgment.
slides.sayZh: 左栏是所有执照级别都做的。高温：移到凉爽处、脱光衣服、空调开到最冷、敷冷湿毛巾、双脚泡冰水，转运前至少降温十分钟，意识下降时测血糖。寒冷：脱掉湿衣服、延长脉搏检查、轻中度主动复温、重度只隔绝保温，以及 AED 最多三次电击的规则。右栏是 PCP 多做的：热病病人有脱水表现时考虑静脉补液；血糖确认低于四时静脉给葡萄糖。低体温流程没有 PCP 独有的步骤，你的价值在于评估和判断。

slides.title: New for you as a PCP: watch out for
slides.body:
• Fluids in heatstroke: listen to the lungs; pulmonary edema can follow
  • Confused athlete who drank a lot? Think low sodium: no oral fluids
  • Endurance athletes: glucose first, lie down; no routine boluses
  • Beta blockers can hide a fast heart rate
  • Cold patient: SpO₂ may not read; check the waveform
  • Cold trauma patient: bleeds more; think hypovolemia protocol early
slides.say: Now that you give fluids and make decisions, here's what's new to watch. In heatstroke, fluids can cause pulmonary edema, so listen to the lungs before and after. A confused runner who drank a lot of water may have low sodium, called exercise-associated hyponatremia, so don't give oral fluids. The book says endurance athletes no longer get automatic fluid loads: check the glucose and let them lie down first. Beta blockers can hide a fast heart rate, so normal vitals may mislead you. In the cold, the pulse oximeter often fails, so check the waveform. And a cold trauma patient bleeds more, so think about the hypovolemia protocol early.
slides.sayZh: 现在你要给液体、要做决定，下面是新的注意事项。热射病补液可能引起肺水肿，所以补液前后都要听肺。喝了很多水、意识混乱的跑者可能是低钠，叫运动相关低钠血症，不要口服补液。原书说耐力赛选手不再常规大量补液：先测血糖，让他们先躺下。β 阻滞剂会掩盖心跳快，所以生命体征正常也可能误导你。寒冷时脉氧仪常读不出来，要看波形。体温低的创伤病人出血更多，要早点想到低血容量流程。

slides.title: For the BC exam
slides.body:
• Heatstroke: book "cool first" → BC: ≥ 10 min before transport
  • Cold VF: book 1 shock → BC: up to 3, then CPR, no pauses
  • Mild hypothermia: book passive → BC: actively rewarm
  • Ambulance: book 28 °C (WMS ≥ 24) → BC: preheat to 30 °C
  • BC grades: mild 32–35, moderate 28–32, severe < 28 °C
  • Book: benzodiazepines for seizures → not in BC EMR/PCP scope
slides.say: For the BC exam, several numbers differ from the book. Heatstroke: the book says cool first, then transport; BC makes it concrete, at least ten minutes before you leave. Hypothermic VF: the book suggests a single shock; BC allows up to three, then CPR without pauses. Mild hypothermia: the book rewarms passively; BC actively rewarms mild and moderate. The ambulance: the book mentions twenty-eight degrees, or at least twenty-four; BC says thirty. For grades, BC uses thirty-five to thirty-two, thirty-two to twenty-eight, and below twenty-eight, not the other system in the book that splits at thirty-four and thirty.
slides.sayZh: BC 考试要注意几个和原书不同的数字。热射病：原书说先降温再转运；BC 说得更具体，出发前至少十分钟。低体温室颤：原书建议只电击一次；BC 允许最多三次，然后不停顿地做 CPR。轻度低体温：原书用被动复温；BC 对轻度和中度都主动复温。救护车温度：原书提到二十八度，或至少二十四度；BC 规定三十度。分级方面，BC 用三十五到三十二、三十二到二十八、低于二十八，而不是原书里以三十四和三十为界的另一套标准。

slides.title: Three things to remember
slides.body:
1. Heatstroke = core > 40 °C + altered mind; cool ≥ 10 min, then go
  2. Frostbite: never rub; never thaw a part that could refreeze
  3. Hypothermia: rewarm mild/moderate; arrest: 3 shocks, then no pauses

Next: drowning, diving and altitude emergencies
slides.say: Three things to remember. One: heatstroke is a core temperature above forty plus an altered mental status, even if the patient is sweating. Cool aggressively for at least ten minutes before transport, then keep cooling, and as a PCP consider fluids for dehydration. Two: never rub frostbite, and never thaw a part that could refreeze. Three: in BC, actively rewarm mild and moderate hypothermia, insulate severe cases, check the pulse for up to forty-five seconds, and in arrest give up to three shocks, then CPR without pauses. Next lesson: drowning, diving and altitude. If anything was unclear, tap Ask. See you next class.
slides.sayZh: 最后记住三件事。一，热射病是核心体温高于四十度加上精神状态改变，即使病人还在出汗。转运前积极降温至少十分钟，路上继续降温；作为 PCP，脱水时考虑补液。二，冻伤绝不搓揉，可能再冻结的部位绝不解冻。三，在 BC，轻度和中度低体温主动复温，重度只保温；脉搏最多查四十五秒；骤停时最多电击三次，之后不停顿地做 CPR。下节课讲溺水、潜水和高原急症。有不懂的点「Ask」。下节课见。
